reviews.title: Serving deliberately misleading ads onto the app screen
reviews.text: First time I’ve opened the app in a while and I was served with an ad on the app’s Home Screen disguised as an app button. There’s a tiny ad marker underneath it, but it’s so small that it’s very easily missed. This is clearly a deliberately misleading ad intended to trick people into clicking. If What3Words are going to serve ads like this, then they need to take some responsibility for preventing this sort of thing. Purely on the basis of this, I’m rating as 1 star and deleting the app from my phone.

reviews.title: Profit over emergency considerations

It’s disappointing because if you ever needed to open the app in an emergency , it feels like they now care more about making profit off you than being the best tool in a crisis.

I appreciate free services need funding, but intrusive adds or a £30 a year subscription for something most people only use a few times or in emergencies is gross. reviews.title: Wasn’t broken so why fix it?
reviews.text:
This WAS an excellent app that had the potential to be lifesaving as well as being so useful.
Then the A.I. moved in.
Up until a few months ago, W3W enabled users to coordinate with Google Maps & other apps.
Now, they want you to subscribe to their own maps & for A.I. to interact with you. So much for the lifesaving element that boasted how various rescue teams were able to use W3W in order to find you accurately in times of emergency. 
I used it regularly as a means to inform drivers in my logistics company to find the right location easily.
Now I’m plagued with irritating, pointless emails from W3W & the system is no longer viable.
Hopefully, this update will be revised & reversed ASAP.

reviews.title: They’ve spammed the app

As a minimum keep the spam but ignore the need to login. Just creates barriers to information in an emergency. Sure you’ll earn less but you won’t be sell outs and will likely save more people who discover that same barrier in a worse situation

reviews.title: Charging stopped me sharing locations
reviews.text:
What3words was absolutely brilliant at simplifying what used to be an OS grid reference and, crucially, allowed locations to be shared with anyone, on any platform, who could then navigate to that point using their chosen navigation app — for free.
That was the entire reason I used it.
Now the only free navigation option is Google Maps. If the recipient doesn’t want to use Google Maps, they’re effectively being asked to subscribe to what3words themselves. At that point, I may as well just send a Google Maps pin in the first place.
What3words has gone from being a genuinely platform- and app-agnostic way of sharing precise locations to little more than a glorified Google Maps shortcut. The subscription doesn’t even solve the real problem — it only fixes things for me, not for my team, my freelancers, or my clients.
Deeply disappointed with how monetisation has been handled here. I’ll be looking for alternatives.

reviews.title: Now almost unusable
reviews.text: The latest version now only offers Apple Maps as a real Navigate option. They also offer Uber, which I guess if you need to find your grocery store is ok. It is totally stupid when navigating a 700+ mile destination. Apple Maps option doesn’t even really give you a route, just pops the neighborhood map of the location. No route, just a duplicate of the  What3words display for the location. Does anyone at the company use their app for anything besides going home from the office?

reviews.title: Voice Over

reviews.title: Wrong free/pro balance
reviews.text:
First of all, w3w is a great idea. It’s been incorporated into most mobile mapping apps to allow searching via w3w. The specificity of position is vital in cases of emergency. 

However, the recent pro upgrade - nothing against apps monetising - has got the balance completely wrong. One basic use case is to gather a list of places and share them. This is now £3.49 per month. Why this isn’t bundled with the free version, I have no idea. The rest of Pro features do genuinely seem to be value added beyond the basic offering, but sharing lists is not. 

I don’t need AI tools or live scans, so I won’t be paying. But that also means I’ll gather my lists in other tools and share them freely, and end up no longer using the app at all. Such a shame.
